output.summary: Two module-level functions gain parameters. tax() in tax.py takes an optional rate (default 0.1), and formatPrice() in src/price.ts takes a required currency. The Python callers order_total and refund now pass 0.2 explicitly, and the TypeScript callers pass 'USD' (aliasCaller reaches formatPrice through a re-export). Several other edits look unrelated: a method call on Calc, a method call on Fmt, a legacy label string, and a config.json currency change that no changed code reads.

groups.title: tax() gains an optional rate parameter
groups.description: The definition replaces the fixed 0.1 factor with a rate argument that defaults to 0.1. Existing one-argument calls keep their behaviour. Read this first.

groups.title: order_total and refund pass a rate of 0.2
groups.description: Both callers now pass 0.2 explicitly. refund calls through the alias t, so check that it refers to the same tax module. Check that 0.2 is the intended rate for both.

groups.title: formatPrice gains a currency parameter
groups.description: The definition now requires a currency string and prefixes the output with it. Any caller that does not pass a currency will break, so check every caller.

groups.title: Callers pass 'USD' to formatPrice
groups.description: Checkout, invoice and receipt summaries pass 'USD' as a literal. aliasCaller calls it through the fmt re-export. Check that a hardcoded 'USD' is intended, since config.json now says EUR.

groups.title: Edits that look unrelated to the signature changes
groups.description: viaMethod calls a formatPrice method on Fmt, which is a different symbol from price.ts. use_calc calls a tax method on Calc, not the module tax(). legacyLabel changes a string and uses the legacy price module. The config.json currency changes from USD to EUR, and no changed code reads it. Confirm each of these is intended.

edgeVerdicts.reason: use_calc calls the tax method of class Calc, which takes one argument. It does not call the module-level tax function.
order_total imports tax from tax.py and calls it directly.
refund calls tax through the namespace import t, which is the tax module imported as t.
checkoutSummary imports formatPrice from ./price.ts and calls it.
viaMethod calls formatPrice on a Fmt instance. Fmt.formatPrice is a different method that takes one argument and is not the function in price.ts.
invoiceSummary imports formatPrice from ./price.ts and calls it.
receiptSummary imports formatPrice from ./price.ts and calls it.
aliasCaller calls fmt, which src/reexport.ts defines as a re-export of formatPrice from ./price.ts under the name fmt.
